name: Non-genetic Central Precocious Puberty in Male
aliases: Idiopathic Central Precocious Puberty in Boys
Early Onset Central Precocious Puberty in Males

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Criteria for Central Precocious Puberty

criteria.description: Onset of secondary sexual characteristics before 9 years of age in males
Elevated luteinizing hormone (LH) response to GnRH stimulation test consistent with pubertal activation
Absence of hypothalamic or pituitary lesions on MRI brain excluding organic causes
Bone age advanced by at least 1 year compared to chronological age
Testicular volume greater than 4 mL indicating pubertal onset

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of early pubertal onset before age 9, pubertal LH response to GnRH stimulation, and exclusion of CNS lesions by imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of genetic and organic causes; idiopathic cases are termed non-genetic.

pathognomonic.notes: Indicative of activation of hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pubertal luteinizing hormone surge on GnRH stimulation
pathognomonic.notes: Diagnostic hallmark differentiating central from peripheral precocious puberty
searchTerms: luteinizing hormone peak during puberty test

pathognomonic.symptomName: Advanced bone age relative to chronological age

common.notes: Early development of secondary sexual characteristics
May be present due to adrenal androgen secretion
Growth acceleration due to sex steroid effects
Result of androgen effects on larynx

occasional.notes: Behavioral changes associated with hormonal fluctuations
Transient breast tissue enlargement due to hormonal imbalance
May occur but usually mild and nonspecific

rare.notes: Suggests possible CNS lesion, rare in non-genetic cases
Very rare, may indicate underlying CNS pathology
Rare in idiopathic cases, more common in organic CPP
searchTerms: neurological and hormonal issues from brain lesion

laboratory: Elevated basal and stimulated luteinizing hormone (LH) levels after GnRH stimulation
Increased testosterone levels consistent with pubertal range
Normal adrenal androgen levels excluding peripheral causes
imaging: Normal MRI of hypothalamic-pituitary region excluding tumors or lesions
genetic: No pathogenic mutations identified in known CPP-associated genes (e.g., MKRN3)
other: Advanced bone age on radiograph of left hand and wrist
Increased testicular volume measured by orchidometer

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of pubertal LH response to GnRH stimulation
Elevated peripheral sex steroids independent of hypothalamic-pituitary axis
Presence of hypothalamic mass on MRI
Earlier onset and more severe neurological symptoms

redFlags: Rapid neurological deterioration or new-onset seizures
Signs of intracranial hypertension or mass effect
references: Carel JC, Leger J. Precocious puberty. N Engl J Med. 2008;358(22):2366-2377.
Kaplowitz PB. Central precocious puberty: update on diagnosis and treatment. Horm Res Paediatr. 2016;85(2):77-85.
Orphanet: Non-genetic central precocious puberty in male. ORPHA:650102.
